purpose: Defines what kind of report BIS is producing, whose evidence it uses, what claims it may make, and what must remain private or unclaimed.
doctrine: A report classification is selected before rendering metrics or narrative.
Numbers are supporting evidence, not the report's meaning.
Competency progression is only reported when an authored competency-to-task mapping and sufficient evidence exist.
Pre/post change is described against the same defined construct or task family; unrelated responses are never treated as a progression score.
No report may infer personality, clinical status, intelligence, employability, permanent mastery or causal programme impact from participation or generic percentages.
Individual private reflections remain outside sponsor and organisation reporting.

classifications.purpose: Explain the learner's journey from starting point through learning, application, investigation, review and next step.
maySay: what the learner demonstrated in defined tasks

classifications.purpose: Summarise evidence against explicitly mapped Applied Commerce competencies.
maySay: highest supported progression level per competency

classifications.purpose: Keep the learner's traceable evidence, revisions, explanations and transfer record across Labs.
maySay: what the learner plans to test next
mustNotSay: that a missing record equals failure
that a derived measure replaces original evidence

classifications.purpose: Show structural progress and support needs without exposing unnecessary private content.
mustNotSay: private hypotheses, reflections or experiment wording unless explicitly shared

classifications.purpose: Describe participation, learning evidence, application coverage and competency evidence across a reportable cohort.
maySay: distribution of supported competency levels when thresholds are met

classifications.purpose: Provide substantive programme results: what was taught, what was practised, what evidence was produced, what competencies were demonstrated, what changed, and what remains unproven.
maySay: evidence-backed progress against defined programme competencies
mustNotSay: causal impact without an appropriate design
certified external competency attainment unless separately verified

classifications.purpose: Assess whether the intended ten-touchpoint curriculum, Lab handoff, evidence windows and reviews were actually delivered.
Show how competency evidence develops across multiple Labs or programme cycles without reducing the learner to a single score.
maySay: which competencies have stronger or broader evidence over time
where evidence moved from explanation to application/test/transfer
mustNotSay: linear progress where evidence is non-comparable
